title: Why Leaves Change Color: Weather and Timing

scenes.title: WEATHER SHAPES THE SHOW
scenes.caption: Temperature and sunlight affect autumn color.
scenes.narration: The calendar is only part of the story. Temperature, sunlight, moisture, and tree health all influence autumn color.

scenes.title: SUNNY DAYS, COOL NIGHTS
scenes.caption: These conditions can boost bright reds.
scenes.narration: For some trees, sunny days help produce sugars while cool nights slow their movement. This can encourage red pigment formation.

scenes.title: CLOUDS AND RAIN
scenes.caption: Wet or warm weather can change the display.
scenes.narration: Cloudy, rainy, or unusually warm weather can affect pigment production and timing. Each autumn is a little different.

scenes.title: DAY LENGTH MATTERS
scenes.caption: Shorter days signal the seasonal shift.
scenes.narration: Trees can sense changing day length. This reliable seasonal cue helps coordinate the transition toward dormancy.

scenes.title: FROST CHANGES THE TIMELINE
scenes.caption: A hard freeze can end the display quickly.
scenes.narration: A strong early frost can damage leaf tissues and shorten the color display. Gentle conditions often allow a longer show.

scenes.title: ONE FOREST, MANY TIMELINES
scenes.caption: Different species respond in different ways.
scenes.narration: Trees do not all change together. Species, elevation, exposure, and local weather create a moving patchwork of color.
